title: 2025 AMC 12B Problem 10
statement: The altitude to the hypotenuse of a \(30\text{-}60\text{-}90\) right triangle is divided into two segments of lengths \(x \lt y\) by the median to the shortest side of the triangle. What is the ratio \(\dfrac{x}{x+y}?\)

solutions.text:
Take \(C = (0,0),\) \(A = (\sqrt{3}, 0),\) \(B = (0, 1),\) so \(AB\) is the hypotenuse and \(BC\) is the shortest side. The altitude from \(C\) meets \(AB\) at \(H = \left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}, \tfrac{3}{4}\right).\) The median from \(A\) to \(M = \left(0, \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\) crosses the altitude at \(P = \left(\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{7}, \tfrac{3}{7}\right).\) This splits the altitude into \(CP = \tfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{7} = \tfrac{4\sqrt{3}}{14}\) and \(PH = \tfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{14},\) so \(x = \tfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{14}\) and \(\dfrac{x}{x+y} = \dfrac{3}{7}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Place the right angle at the origin with the legs along the axes and coordinatize every point
Find where the median to the shortest side crosses the altitude to the hypotenuse, then split the altitude at that point
